name: The Somnolent Grove

detectability.signature: Electrochemical ripple at sleeping-cortex frequencies, wrapped in a ghostly green glow

proximity: Crew share stray daydreams across decks before the airlock even cycles
Sleep aboard grows vivid, shared, and strangely restful
contact: Memories surface that belong to no one aboard as identity bleed begins
Instruments record dream-spindle activity mirroring the crew's own brainwaves
prolonged_exposure: Personalities dissolve into the field's slow consensus; bodies are found placid, minds absent
Consciousness transfer into the field leaves crews alive but no longer themselves

phenomena: Psychic pressure or telepathic interference at all depths of the field
Electromagnetic patterns resembling neural activity rippling through empty space
Bioluminescent green radiance with no found source
hazards: Consciousness transfer or loss during prolonged exposure
Psychic attack or mental influence on sensitive crew
Crew behavioral changes toward placid compliance
opportunities: Communication with other dimensions or times through structured dialogue attempts
Contact with alien intelligence embedded in the field
Data valuable to scientific institutions studying consciousness itself
known_incidents: The research cutter Quiet Husbandry was found adrift at its center, crew alive and seated calmly at their stations, unable to recall their own names
description: Ghostly green radiance fills a quarter-AU sphere like moonlight through an orchard in leaf, though no matter has ever been found within it. Electrochemical patterns ripple through the volume at exactly the frequencies of a sleeping cortex. Crews describe the sensation of standing in a garden tended by someone just out of sight.

The Grove breathes on a slow thirty-one-hour wave, brightness swelling as if in dreams. Ships entering share stray daydreams across their decks before the airlock even cycles. Longer stays blur the borders between minds: memories surface that belong to no one aboard.

The research cutter Quiet Husbandry was found adrift at its center, her crew seated calmly at their stations, alive, and unable to recall their own names. Recovery teams returned most of those minds over eighteen months of therapy. The Grove itself has never been observed doing anything but dreaming.

Institutions maintain a listening abbey at its boundary where volunteers, carefully rotated, attempt structured dialogue with the field. Fragments retrieved so far include mathematics, lullabies, and what may be an apology. Travelers with nowhere else to be are asked to pass quietly.
